question:
A 64-year-old male waiter comes to the emergency department with bilateral calf swelling and dull,
aching pain that began three days ago and has progressively worsened. His medical history is
significant for four previous deep vein thromboses (three in lower extremities, one in upper extremity).
He takes no medications and denies alcohol or tobacco use. His vital signs show: temperature 37.3 ºC
(99.1 ºF), heart rate 84/min, respiratory rate 17/min, and blood pressure 131/97 mmHg. Physical
examination reveals bilateral leg edema with mild erythema and tenderness. Doppler ultrasound
confirms bilateral infrapopliteal deep vein thromboses. After receiving subcutaneous enoxaparin and
initial bloodwork, which of the following tests would be most appropriate to include in the diagnostic
evaluation? Answer Choices: (A) Prothrombin activity level now (B) Antinuclear antibody now (C)
Factor V Leiden mutation testing now (D) Anticardiolipin antibody now and in three months, regardless
of initial test results (E) D-dimer level now and in four months (F) Protein S activity level now while on

anticoagulation (G) Prothrombin activity level in four months (H) Protein C activity level in four months
(I) Antithrombin III activity level in two months (J) Homocysteine level after three months of
anticoagulation
 A. Antithrombin III activity level in two months
B. Antinuclear antibody now
C. Protein C activity level in four months
D. Anticardiolipin antibody now and in three months, regardless of initial test results
E. Protein S activity level now while on anticoagulation
F. Prothrombin activity level in four months
G. D-dimer level now and in four months
H. Homocysteine level after three months of anticoagulation
I. Prothrombin activity level now
J. Factor V Leiden mutation testing now
